candidates.name: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
support_spans: intractable mucocutaneous lesions
Skin biopsy revealed spongiosis and numerous neutrophils with nuclear dust in the epidermis and superficial perivascular dermatitis with predominant infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis.
Immunoblotting of normal human epidermal extract: Positive for IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin (210 kDa) and periplakin (190 kDa)
contradict_spans: No swollen cervical and axillary lymph nodes were palpable.
Chest, abdomen, and pelvic computed tomography showed no abnormalities.
candidates.why: The presence of intractable mucocutaneous lesions, specific histopathological features, and positive immunoblotting results for autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin are characteristic of paraneoplastic pemphigus.

candidates.name: Pemphigus vulgaris
support_spans: Small bullae, erosions, and crusts were present on the lower lip.
Erosions with epithelized mucosa were observed in the oral cavity.
Flaccid discrete and coalesced bullae, crusts, and erosions over erythematous and cicatricial lesions were present on the face, trunk, and extremities.
contradict_spans: Direct immunofluorescence (IF): No obvious deposits of IgG, IgA, and C3 to either the epithelial cell surface or the basement membrane zone
Chemiluminescent enzyme immunoassays: Negative for Dsg1, Dsg3, and BP180 16th noncollagenous domain
candidates.why: The clinical presentation of flaccid bullae and erosions on the skin and mucous membranes is consistent with pemphigus vulgaris, but the negative immunological studies contradict this diagnosis.
